guard: A scope's failure record keeps a classified refusal's own code (#1519): a RuntimeFault the program caused settles under its catalog code with kind `runtime`, a plain handler throw stays the generic L4000 scope-fault, and a handler's own EffectError keeps its code and kind. Live and resume then read the same code.
why: One settle site, three arms, and a mutation per arm: reverting the RuntimeFault arm to the flattening form is the exact pre-fix expression; dropping the EffectError arm kills the preserved-code control; dropping the RuntimeFault class check makes every plain throw mint a bogus catalog code and kills the L4000 control.

mutations.name: the scope settle flattens a program's RuntimeFault back to the generic L4000
mutations.expectRed: a program refusal raised inside a scope settles under its own catalog code, not the generic L4000
mutations.completionMarker: a handler fault records the STACK of the error that was thrown, read back off the recorded entry
mutations.cell: a program refusal raised inside a scope settles under its own catalog code, not the generic L4000
mutations.note: The exact pre-fix expression. With it back, the record says L4000 scope-fault with the L3021 sentence inside the message, and the resume cell reads L4000 where the live run caught L3021.

mutations.name: the resume half is left reading the flattened record
mutations.expectRed: and a resume over the same journal reads the SAME code the live run caught, not a flattened L4000
mutations.completionMarker: a handler fault records the STACK of the error that was thrown, read back off the recorded entry
mutations.cell: and a resume over the same journal reads the SAME code the live run caught, not a flattened L4000
mutations.note: Same revert, different named assertion: the resume cell is the observable harm (#1519's real traffic), and proving it red separately pins the replay path to the record.

mutations.name: the EffectError arm is dropped and every handler failure flattens
mutations.find:
reason instanceof EffectError
        ? recordableError(reason, "scope-fault").error
        : reason instanceof RuntimeFault
mutations.expectRed: and a handler's own coded failure keeps its code and kind through the same settle
mutations.completionMarker: a handler fault records the STACK of the error that was thrown, read back off the recorded entry
mutations.cell: and a handler's own coded failure keeps its code and kind through the same settle
mutations.note: The control that the fix did not eat the EffectError path: with the arm disabled, a coded L6002 handler failure records as L4000 scope-fault and the control goes red.

mutations.name: the class check is dropped and a plain throw mints the thrown message's code
mutations.replace: : { code: (reason as { code?: unknown })?.code as string ?? "L4000", kind: "runtime", message: messageOf(reason) };
mutations.expectRed: a handler's plain throw inside a scope still settles as the generic L4000 scope-fault, unchanged by the program-refusal rule
mutations.completionMarker: a handler fault records the STACK of the error that was thrown, read back off the recorded entry
mutations.cell: a handler's plain throw inside a scope still settles as the generic L4000 scope-fault, unchanged by the program-refusal rule
mutations.note: The other direction of the fence: trusting any thrown object's `code` field (an errno, an HTTP status) would record unclassified failures under codes the catalog never gave them.
